data.name: Aksh
data.gender_notes: Aksh is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Sanskrit word ‘aksh’, meaning ‘radiant’, ‘shining’, or ‘eye’. In Hindu mythology, Aksh is also the name of a sage and a deity associated with vision and wisdom. The name Aksh carries the meaning “Radiant, Shining” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Aksh usually hope their child will grow to embody radiant, shining and live with faith, good character and purpose.

historical_references.reference: Akshapada or Akshapatta was a legendary king of the Vatsa dynasty, located in the present-day Uttar Pradesh, India. He is known for his military prowess and is mentioned in several ancient Indian texts including the Mahabharata and the Puranas. Akshapada is believed to have ruled during the 5th century BCE.

Aksh is also a common personal name in Hindu culture. The name Aksh is derived from the Sanskrit word 'Akshara', which means 'imperishable' or 'indestructible'. It is believed that the name was given to children born during auspicious occasions, and was considered a symbol of good luck and prosperity.
